input.quote: 12.3 Nothing restricts Customer from developing, acquiring, licensing, selling, or using any product or service, engaging any supplier, hiring any person who responds to general recruitment, or conducting business in any field or territory. Vendor acknowledges that Customer has made no exclusivity, non-compete, most-favoured-customer, minimum-volume, or no-hire commitment.
input.rationale: Section 12.3 expressly preserves Customer's freedom to develop, acquire, licence, sell, or use any product or service and to conduct business in any field or territory, and records that Customer has given no non-compete commitment, so the preferred position (no non-compete or field-of-use restriction on Customer) is met on the document's face. No other clause binds Customer's business: §2.1 confirms there is no minimum quantity or purchase commitment, §13.1 is a non-exclusive grant to Customer, and §13.4 is a narrow acceptable-use restriction (reverse engineering, interference, security bypass, unlawful use) rather than a competitive or field-of-use covenant. The sole-and-exclusive-provider language in §2.2 is a sourcing exclusivity that we review under the exclusivity rule; it does not restrict Customer's own products, brand, or lines of business, and we do not flag it twice here.
